subject: ‘Good job!’: the Election Commission and the press, propping each other up
alt: Sandeep Adhwaryu's cartoon: on the left of a white page stands an elderly man with grey hair and glasses, in a grey suit, white shirt and orange tie; in his left hand is a brown briefcase marked ECI, and his right hand is raised in a thumbs-up. He is smiling. Above, a black band carries the words #NATIONALPRESSDAY in white, and below it three hand-lettered lines: GOOD JOB! INSTITUTIONS MUST STAND BY EACH OTHER, with a small line running from the words to the man. On the right stand two journalists: in front a woman with short hair in a pink dress, holding a red microphone with a red square logo and a white mark; behind her a man in glasses and a pale green shirt, holding a blue and white microphone. Both are smiling. The cartoonist's signature, Adhwaryu, is at the lower right.
chutki: On National Press Day the head of the Election Commission stands with a briefcase marked ECI and gives the reporters a thumbs-up: good job! Institutions must stand by each other.

The needle is in that ‘each other’. In a democracy institutions do not pat each other's backs; they watch each other - the press watches power, the Commission watches the cleanliness of the election. The day the two start saying ‘good job’ to each other, who will ask the questions?
